author: Ash

copy.intro: The Akira dress you wanted for Saturday just sold out in your size, or the nearest Akira is a state away. It started as one Chicago boutique in 2002 and now has more than 40 stores, with dresses from $29.90 to $299.90 and most under $100. Every store here sells dresses to US shoppers. The ones named most often next to Akira come first, then the closest on price.

bodies.venus:
Venus is the closest match on price. Its full-price dresses run from $39 to $168, and nearly all of them cost under $100. Start with the Velvet Cowl Neck Midi Dress ($79), a little under what a typical Akira dress costs.

It began in 1982 as a swimwear label in Jacksonville, Florida, and swim still leads its homepage. Its dress edits are named for vacations and wedding guests. Sizes run 2 to 24, and some dresses come in petite.

Returns cost you, though. You get 30 days, but a $9 fee comes off your refund unless you paid for its Checkout+ add-on, and it only ships within the US. For louder going-out pieces, Dolls Kill is the better call.
bodies.sabo:
SABO is the step up from Akira on price, with full-price dresses from $67.86 to $416.52. The Dimmi Dress ($74.88) is one of the cheapest ways in. Most of its dresses cost more than a typical Akira one, and the top of the range is Zaco, a second label sold on the same site.

It's a Brisbane label founded in 2011, and its own pieces are designed in-house. The US store prices in dollars with duties already included, so there's nothing extra to pay when the box arrives. Shipping is free over $175. Sizes run 2XS to 3XL, which works out to US 0 to 14.

Returns are the trade-off. You have 14 days from delivery to post them back, and the $20 return label comes out of your refund. If you want longer to decide, Windsor gives you 30 days.
bodies.pink-ice:
Pink Ice is the cheaper way into the same look, and no full-price dress on the site goes past $89.99. The Rachel Ribbed Mini Dress ($17.99) costs less than Akira's cheapest dress, and the Palm Beach Maxi Dress ($39.99) is a fair middle pick.

It's a Los Angeles online boutique that stocks other labels. Check the label names before you buy. Love Stitch and Flying Tomato make more than half of its dresses. AMI Clubwear sells Flying Tomato too, so compare the two if a style turns up at both. US shipping is free over $50, and refunds go back to how you paid within 30 days of shipping.

Dresses stop at Large, though, a long way short of Akira's 3X. Venus and AMI Clubwear go much further.
bodies.amiclubwear:
AMI Clubwear covers Akira's club-night side, and its dress prices start lower than anywhere else here. Full-price dresses run from $11.50 to $125.99, and the Tempting Me Print Mini Dress ($64) is an easy place to start.

It's a Los Angeles shop, and most of its dresses come from Flying Tomato, the same label Pink Ice carries. Sizes go S to 3X, which matches Akira's top size. Free standard shipping to the lower 48 states needs the code FREESHIP at checkout.

The catch is getting money back. Returns within 30 days of receipt are for store credit only, and you pay the postage. If a refund to your card matters, Pink Ice or Venus are the safer bets.
bodies.dollskill:
Dolls Kill suits the bolder end of Akira, with its own house labels like Widow and Club Exx sold next to brands it stocks. The Club Exx Sensory Escapade Bodycon Dress ($59) is a good example of the going-out side.

Most of its dresses carry a markdown, so start on the sale rail rather than the new arrivals. Women's sizes run XXS to 3X, the same top size as Akira, and US shipping is free over $50. It's been selling since 2011 out of San Francisco.

Every return comes back as a gift card, never a refund. AMI Clubwear only gives store credit too, so if you want your money back, Tiger Mist or Pink Ice are better.
bodies.windsor:
Windsor is the pick if you'd rather try a dress on in a store, with more than 350 of them. Full-price dresses run from $14 to $199.90, and the Naya Lace-Up High Slit Sequin Column Dress ($79.90) shows the formal side it's known for.

Like Akira, it ships free over $75 and gives you 30 days to return. It's been focused on special-occasion dresses since 1957, so it's the stop for homecoming and prom.

It falls short on size. Dresses stop at XL, a US 15, where Akira goes to 3X. For a bigger size with a store to visit, Princess Polly runs to a US 20 in its Curve line.
bodies.for-love-lemons:
For Love & Lemons is the splurge, for when the dress is the whole point of the night. The Abby Mini Dress ($239) costs about what Akira's priciest minis do, and its maxi dresses go higher. The range runs from minis to full gowns, like the Morrigan Gown.

Laura Hall and Gillian Rose Kern founded it in 2010, and it sells itself on flattering cuts and detail work. Sizes run XXS to XL, and US shipping is free over $250, which one Abby nearly covers.

But returns are tight. You get 21 days from when the order ships, and a flat $10 fee for US returns. If you want designer dresses with free returns, Revolve is the better fit.
bodies.princess-polly:
Princess Polly is the closest thing to Akira's under-$100 dresses. Full-price dresses run from $49 to $119, and nearly all of them come in under $100. The Celena Mini Dress ($58) is a good one to start with.

It started online on Australia's Gold Coast in 2010 and now has US stores in Arizona, California, Massachusetts and Ohio, so some of you can try before you buy. Core sizes run US 0 to 12, and the Curve line goes from 14 to 20. Shipping is free over $50, a lower bar than Akira's $75, and you get 30 days to return for a refund, exchange or gift card.

Curve stops at a US 20, though, and Akira's 3X is a 26 to 28. Venus goes to a 24.
bodies.pink-lily:
Pink Lily is the one for everyday dresses at Akira's lower prices. Every full-price dress sits between $38 and $78. The Garden Gypsy Multi Floral Mini Dress ($58) lands right in the middle.

It's a Bowling Green, Kentucky boutique started by Tori Gerbig, and it mixes its own designs with labels like Maize and Tailoria. Florals and minis make up a lot of it, with a few sweater and tee dresses. Shipping is free over $79. Returns within 30 days of shipping are free if you take store credit, and a refund costs $7.95.

Sizes stop at XL, and the mix is more daytime than Akira's. For a night-out dress at a similar price, Princess Polly or Pink Ice fit better.
bodies.tiger-mist:
Tiger Mist is a good match for the minis Akira does well, and most of its dresses are exactly that. Full-price dresses run from $69 to $139. The Midori Metallic Bandage Mini Dress ($105) is the party pick, and the Cleo Mini Dress ($79) is the simpler one. The Sasha Crochet Mini Dress ($139) is where the range tops out.

Its US store prices in dollars and ships free over $75, the same line as Akira. Returns run 30 days. Take store credit and the label is free, or take a refund and $10 comes off.

Sizes go XXS to XL, so skip it if you need a plus size. AMI Clubwear has club minis up to 3X.
bodies.forever-21:
Forever 21 is the cheapest pick, with full-price dresses at $24.99, under Akira's $29.90 floor. The Satin Lace Cutout Mini Dress ($24.99) is one of them, and the one price across the rail makes budgeting easy.

It's LA-born and closed its US stores in 2025, so it's online only now. Sizes run XS to XXL, with a plus section on top. US shipping is free over $50, and you can return within 30 days for a refund, minus a $9.99 return fee.

The full-price rail is small, though. Most of its dresses are marked down, and clearance and final-sale items can't go back. Check whether a dress is final sale before you buy.
bodies.fashion-nova:
Fashion Nova is the one to try if you shop Akira's extended sizes, because it has a whole Plus+Curve section. It started in 2006 as one Los Angeles store and is based in Beverly Hills now.

Most dresses show a sale price beside a higher Comp. Value. So judge each one by the price you'd pay, not the discount, and compare it with Akira's typical $89.90.

Shipping is free over $75, the same as Akira, and it also ships to Canada, the UK and Australia. If you'd rather see the clothes first, Windsor and Princess Polly have stores.
bodies.revolve:
Revolve is the designer end of this list, for when you want a brand name on the dress. Its dress page runs from the LIONESS Original Sin Dress ($69) to gowns like the MAJORELLE Tracy Gown ($328), past Akira's $299.90 top. The LIONESS Stars Align Mini Dress ($79) is another easy entry.

Shipping and returns are free. You get 30 days for a refund and 60 for an exchange. Sizes run XXS to 4X, US 00 to 24/26.

It stocks a lot of labels, so start with LIONESS if you want Akira-style minis at Akira prices. For one designer label you can buy direct, For Love & Lemons is the alternative.
bodies.nordstrom:
Nordstrom is the department-store route, and the easiest on returns. Shipping is free across the US with no minimum, and there's no time limit on returns. The Petal & Pup Laurel A-Line Dress ($89) and the Baltic Børn Veronica Velvet Maxi Dress ($65) sit in Akira's price range. ASTR the Label's Abrianna Lace Trim Satin Midi Dress ($138) is a step up.

It carries labels like Adrianna Papell and Dress the Population, so it's a good bet for wedding-guest and cocktail dresses. With more than 350 locations across Nordstrom, Nordstrom Local and Nordstrom Rack, you can usually try a dress on before you commit.

For club minis, though, it's not the obvious first stop. AMI Clubwear or Dolls Kill are closer to that.

closing.heading: How to choose
closing.body:
Start with your budget. Under $90, Pink Ice and Pink Lily keep everything below that line, and Forever 21 goes under $25. Around Akira's typical $90, Venus and Princess Polly are the closest match. If you're spending more, SABO and For Love & Lemons are the step up, and Revolve has the designer labels.

Then check your size. AMI Clubwear and Dolls Kill both reach Akira's 3X, and Venus goes to a 24. Want to try it on first? Windsor and Nordstrom have the most stores. And if getting your money back matters, skip AMI Clubwear and Dolls Kill, which only give store credit or gift cards.

faqs.a: Yes. It's a Chicago company that opened its first boutique in 2002 and now has more than 40 stores in over 18 states. Online orders can go back within 30 days of the order date.

faqs.q: What does the name Akira mean?
faqs.a: For the store, it's co-founder Erikka Wang's first name spelled backwards, with a few letters switched around.
